Of Composites, Dayton, Oct. 2025 5.2 Recommendations for future work: Based on the work done and the findings, following tasks are recommended to advance this technology further: 1. Create a committee to generate comprehensive standards for (i) composite materials under cryogenic conditions, and (ii) aviation/ground transport operational and safety conditions for liquid Hydrogen tanks. These exist in parts and are scattered. This is an industry-wide requirement. 2. Develop an open-source approach to cryogenic material characterization methods and modeling methods for composite components for long-term damage and durability (i.e. for decades of service). These should include material testing standards, acceptance criteria, reliability and confidence limits. 3. Complete Phase 1 and Phase 2 Tasks of this program: • Mank and boss design, with updated parameters from manufacturing • Manufacture and assemble full cryogenic tank i.e. outer tank, inner tank, MLI and bosses/tubes • Perform boil-off and burst pressure testing of tank • Complete Design and manufacture full Conformal tank 4. Simulate tank response under actual service conditions: • Analyze tank response under actual vehicular service conditions i.e. regular service condition (fatigue, vibration, etc.) and safety-critical scenarios. • Material characterization for long-term response (years to a decade) durability 5.
